results.name: dvd_antisymm_of_normalize_eq
results.source_text:
theorem dvd_antisymm_of_normalize_eq {a b : α} (ha : normalize a = a) (hb : normalize b = b)
    (hab : a ∣ b) (hba : b ∣ a) : a = b :=
  ha ▸ hb ▸ normalize_eq_normalize hab hba

results.name: dvd_antisymm
results.source_text:
theorem dvd_antisymm : a ∣ b → b ∣ a → a = b := by
  rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩ ⟨d, hcd⟩
  rw [mul_assoc, eq_comm, mul_right_eq_self₀, mul_eq_one] at hcd
  obtain ⟨rfl, -⟩ | rfl := hcd <;> simp

results.name: normalize
results.source_text:
/-- Chooses an element of each associate class, by multiplying by `normUnit` -/
def normalize (x : α) : α := x * normUnit x
results.docstring: Chooses an element of each associate class, by multiplying by `normUnit`

results.name: dvd_antisymm'
results.source_text:
theorem dvd_antisymm' : a ∣ b → b ∣ a → b = a :=
  flip dvd_antisymm

@[simp]
theorem normalize_neg (x : V) : normalize (-x) = - normalize x := by
  simp [normalize]

results.name: CKMMatrix.snd_row_normalized_normSq

/-- The absolute value squared of the second row of a CKM matrix is `1`, in terms of `nomSq`. -/
lemma snd_row_normalized_normSq (V : CKMMatrix) :
    normSq [V]cd + normSq [V]cs + normSq [V]cb = 1 := by
  repeat rw [← Complex.sq_norm]
  exact V.snd_row_normalized_abs
results.docstring: The absolute value squared of the second row of a CKM matrix is `1`, in terms of `nomSq`.

  VAbs_sum_sq_row_eq_one ⟦V⟧ 1

results.name: EuclideanDomain.dvd_gcd
results.source_text:
theorem dvd_gcd {a b c : R} : c ∣ a → c ∣ b → c ∣ gcd a b :=
  GCD.induction a b (fun _ _ H => by simpa only [gcd_zero_left] using H) fun a b _ IH ca cb => by
    rw [gcd_val]
    exact IH ((dvd_mod_iff ca).2 cb) ca

results.name: EuclideanDomain.gcd
results.source_text:
/-- `gcd a b` is a (non-unique) element such that `gcd a b ∣ a` `gcd a b ∣ b`, and for
  any element `c` such that `c ∣ a` and `c ∣ b`, then `c ∣ gcd a b` -/
def gcd (a b : R) : R :=
  if a0 : a = 0 then b
  else
    have _ := mod_lt b a0
    gcd (b % a) a
termination_by a
results.docstring:
`gcd a b` is a (non-unique) element such that `gcd a b ∣ a` `gcd a b ∣ b`, and for
any element `c` such that `c ∣ a` and `c ∣ b`, then `c ∣ gcd a b`

results.name: EuclideanDomain.gcdMonoid
results.source_text:
/-- Create a `GCDMonoid` whose `GCDMonoid.gcd` matches `EuclideanDomain.gcd`. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
def gcdMonoid (R) [EuclideanDomain R] [DecidableEq R] : GCDMonoid R where
  gcd := gcd
  lcm := lcm
  gcd_dvd_left := gcd_dvd_left
  gcd_dvd_right := gcd_dvd_right
  dvd_gcd := dvd_gcd
  gcd_mul_lcm a b := by rw [EuclideanDomain.gcd_mul_lcm]; rfl
  lcm_zero_left := lcm_zero_left
  lcm_zero_right := lcm_zero_right

results.name: EuclideanDomain.gcd_dvd
results.source_text:
theorem gcd_dvd (a b : R) : gcd a b ∣ a ∧ gcd a b ∣ b :=
  GCD.induction a b
    (fun b => by
      rw [gcd_zero_left]
      exact ⟨dvd_zero _, dvd_rfl⟩)
    fun a b _ ⟨IH₁, IH₂⟩ => by
    rw [gcd_val]
    exact ⟨IH₂, (dvd_mod_iff IH₂).1 IH₁⟩

results.name: EuclideanDomain.gcd_dvd_left
results.source_text:
theorem gcd_dvd_left (a b : R) : gcd a b ∣ a :=
  (gcd_dvd a b).left

results.name: EuclideanGroup
results.source_text:
/-- An n-dimensional `Euclidean group` is a group of
rotations, reflections, and translations.
-/
@[ext]
structure EuclideanGroup (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The translation part of a Euclidean transformation. -/
  translation : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
  /-- The orthogonal linear part of a Euclidean transformation. -/
  linear : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ
results.docstring:
An n-dimensional `Euclidean group` is a group of
rotations, reflections, and translations.
